sections.h2: Your options for selling a North Bergen house
sections.html:
North Bergen sellers weigh an agent's listing against a private sale or a straight as-is purchase, and the best fit turns on tenants, a hillside lot and any open code issues. The township covers 5.14 square miles of land and has an estimated 61,483 residents, which is 3.0% fewer than its 2020 base. Owners occupy about 41.6% of homes, and the median value is $473,500.

Before you choose, assemble what a buyer's attorney and the title company will ask for.

  • The deed and your latest tax bill.
  • Any certificate of occupancy for the building and its legal unit count.
  • Rent control registration if any unit is rented.
  • Lease copies and rent ledgers for each tenant.

sections.h2: Hills, flood zones and what buyers inspect
sections.html:
The township is shaped like an inverted L, with the Hudson River on its eastern edge facing Manhattan and the Hackensack River on the west toward Carlstadt. The Palisades rise from the waterfront, and a steep slope on the west side drops toward the Meadowlands.

Steep driveways, retaining walls and stairs up to the front door are features a buyer will want to inspect, so photograph and describe them honestly. Low-lying ground on the west side is part of the New Jersey Meadowlands, so ask your insurance agent whether your parcel sits in a flood zone before you quote a closing date.

Of 64.74 miles of road, the township maintains 50.00, Hudson County 7.85, the state 5.49 and the Turnpike Authority 1.40, so a complaint about a street goes to a different office depending on who owns it.

sections.h2: Neighborhoods to name in a listing
sections.html:
Name the section, since housing type and transit access vary across the township.

  • Bergenline Avenue, a commercial strip with more than 300 stores and restaurants.
  • The Racetrack section, on the plateau between Bergenline Avenue and Kennedy Boulevard.
  • Bergenwood, clinging to the west-facing slope of the Palisades.
  • New Durham, near the Bergen Turnpike and Tonnelle Avenue.
  • Meadowview behind the Municipal Building, and Babbitt out in the Meadowlands.
  • Bulls Ferry and Woodcliff, toward the Hudson and North Hudson Park.

About 71.4% of residents are Hispanic or Latino and 74.5% of residents age 5 and up speak another language at home, so Spanish-language listings can reach a large share of local buyers.

Commuters buy here for buses and light rail. Route 495 links the Lincoln Tunnel with the Turnpike, and NJ Transit lines such as the 121, 125, 127 and 128 terminate at Midtown Manhattan's Port Authority terminal. Jitneys on Bergenline Avenue can run as often as one a minute. The Hudson-Bergen Light Rail stops at Tonnelle Avenue and reaches Weehawken, Hoboken, Jersey City and Bayonne.

Residents take 33.1 minutes on average to reach work, so a block near a bus line or a light rail stop is worth highlighting in your description.

The township runs its own rent control program, and its office explains which apartments are covered, the legal base rent, capital improvement surcharges and annual registration. Files on residential properties are open for public inspection. The yearly increase is 2.5 percent of base rent, allowed once in any twelve months, with at least 30 days' notice to tenants after approval.

Renovations go through the Rent Control office, with inspections before and after. Ask the office whether your building is covered before you hand a buyer a rent roll.

Short-term rentals are tightly restricted. Ordinance 610-23, adopted September 20, 2023, bars them for anyone who had not registered a dwelling by September 6, 2023. Do not market a house on the strength of Airbnb income unless it already holds a registration certificate.

sections.h2: Code Enforcement and certificates of occupancy
sections.html:
The township's Code Enforcement office inspects and issues residential and commercial certificates of occupancy, and it investigates illegal occupancy. The number is 201-392-2051. The township website also lists a Residential Owner Certificate form and an illegal apartment hotline, so ask whether any unit count in your deed differs from what is actually in the building.

If a mortgage goes into default, Ordinance 325-17 has the lender inspect the house and register it with the Building Department within 10 days, stating whether it is vacant or occupied. Owners facing default can ask that department how the registration works.

sections.h2: Fees, forms and the Hudson County recording office
sections.html:
The state's realty transfer fee falls on the seller. A deed from an executor or administrator to an heir or devisee under a will or intestacy law is exempt, which helps with inherited houses, and so is a deed recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree. Prices above $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee, 1% up to $2,000,000 and more above that.

A seller or heir who lives out of state prepays at least 2% of the deed price toward state income tax. The estimate is 10.75% of the gain when that comes out higher.

Hudson County deeds go to the Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages at 257 Cornelison Avenue, second floor, in Jersey City. Cashier and search hours run weekdays from 9:00 am to 2:00 pm, and phones are answered from 8:00 am to 3:45 pm at 201-395-4760. The Register also runs a free Recording Notification Service that warns owners when a document is filed against their property.

Start with paper. Pull the deed, the tax bill, the certificate of occupancy and, for rentals, the rent control registration and leases. Call Code Enforcement if the unit count in the deed may not match the building, because an unapproved apartment is easier to deal with before an offer than after one. Keep the lease copies and rent ledgers where you can find them, since a buyer's attorney will ask for them in the first week.

Next, decide how the house will be sold. A buyer paying cash can take it with its flaws, including hillside stairs or an old addition, and can often close on your schedule. A buyer relying on a mortgage brings an appraisal and a lender's checklist. Whichever you choose, your attorney or title company files the deed and the seller's residency form at the Hudson County office in Jersey City.

faqs.q: Is a North Bergen house with an unapproved apartment sellable?
faqs.a: A sale can go ahead, but tell buyers up front. The township's Code Enforcement office investigates illegal occupancy and keeps an illegal apartment hotline, so call 201-392-2051 and ask what a buyer or lender will need before closing.

Yes. The Rent Control office administers the ordinance, which allows an annual increase of 2.5 percent of base rent, once in twelve months, with at least 30 days' notice to tenants. Covered rentals must register.

faqs.q: May a buyer turn my house into an Airbnb?
faqs.a: Generally no. Ordinance 610-23 ended new short-term rental registrations after September 6, 2023, and only dwellings holding a registration certificate by then are grandfathered. Confirm with the township before advertising it that way.

faqs.q: Is the transfer fee owed on an inherited house?
faqs.a: Not on the executor's deed that moves the house to an heir under the will or intestacy law. If the heir then sells to a buyer, that second deed is a sale and the fee applies to it.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for North Bergen property?
faqs.a: The Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, 257 Cornelison Avenue, second floor, Jersey City. Your title company or attorney normally files it with the fee affidavit and the seller's residency form.
